column11: 0.5 x the fitted PCSK9 anchor, against lly_solbinsiran.csv's 0.25, and the difference IS the judgement. The anchor is the same: the PCSK9 inhibitors, the last high-priced injectable lipid class to launch into a prevalent US pool against payer prior authorisation. In Cardiology Consultants of Philadelphia, 97 cardiologists (Smith A et al., J Clin Med 2021;10:3828, doi 10.3390/jcm10173828, PMC8432238, Table 2), the yearly share of eligible ASCVD patients newly prescribed one was 0.26% in 2015 (from the July launch), 1.23% in 2016, 1.09% in 2017, 1.52% in 2018 and 1.60% in 2019, which a logistic of peak 0.0142, k 3.06 and midpoint -0.55 fits to an rmse of 0.17 points. 0.5 x 0.0142 = 0.0071. WHY DOUBLE SOLBINSIRAN'S MULTIPLE: the solbinsiran seed sets 0.25 on the explicit ground that solbinsiran 'would be the third RNA drug into sHTG after olezarsen (approved June 2026) and plozasiran, both APOC3, which cut triglycerides by about 80% in sHTG (SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 medians of 79% and 81%, Arrowhead 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30) against solbinsiran's 58% to 60% in mixed dyslipidaemia'. Plozasiran IS the drug that seed names as arriving ahead of it with the better effect, and it is second rather than third
column12: Arrowhead's own 10-K confirms the readout the multiple leans on: 'Arrowhead presented results from the pivotal Phase 3 SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 studies of plozasiran in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG)' and 'SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 met their primary and all prespecified secondary endpoints and demonstrated deep and durable reductions in TGs, with median reductions from baseline of 79% and 81%, respectively, at Month 12 (p<0.0001 in both studies)' (ARWR FY2026 10-K, arwr-20260930.htm). Against the multiple: olezarsen was approved in sHTG in June 2026 and is quarterly-dosed too, so plozasiran enters second, not first; and every sHTG entrant faces the same prior-authorisation wall the PCSK9 series measures

column12: THE RANGE IS TENFOLD AND THE TOP OF IT IS TAKEN ON PURPOSE: at 1 per million the overlap would be 0.000478 and the expansion worth 0.43% more. Choosing the top means this row cannot flatter the readout. Neither end changes the valuation materially, which is itself the finding - FCS is a rounding error against severe hypertriglyceridemia, and essentially all of Redemplo's value sits in the sHTG expansion this catalyst gates. column11: comparator estimate: Novartis's charge as nvs_leqvio.csv carries it, word for word, so growth_investment reads the same restatements off it. derived and found to be nil: NVS's filed expense lines already leave less than the 31.44% of revenue it turned into free cash over 2023 to 2025, so there is nothing left to charge. Restated before interest: NVS paid $2,587mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.72% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so adding it back only widens a gap the filed lines already leave, and the charge stays nil. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 30.05% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 37.20%, so the charge rebuilds at -7.15%. It was held at nil, but NVS books $3,197mm of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001114448-26-000004), 5.86% of revenue, so the charge stops at that floor: -5.86%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 NVS's cash flow statement shows receivables up $3,559mm, inventories up $737mm, payables up $101mm, a working capital build of $4,195mm, 2.79% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at the amortisation floor, -5.86% where the filed figures rebuild it at -7.15%, and stays there. Struck on total revenue: Novartis's filed cost lines sit against net sales of USD 54,532mm and other revenues of USD 2,142mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001114448-26-000004, Note 4), and the income statement shows other revenues above cost of goods sold with no cost of their own, so each ratio is scaled by 54,532 over 56,674 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3269 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3911 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -5.8626%.

column11: Arrowhead's own US list price less the book's Part D gross-to-net convention. List: 'Updated the U.S. wholesale acquisition cost (WAC) of REDEMPLO to $45,000 per patient per year' and 'As part of the One-REDEMPLO unified pricing model, the new price is intended to remain consistent across FCS and severe hypertriglyceridemia (SHTG), if that indication is approved' (Arrowhead fiscal 2026 second quarter release, 2026-05-07, 8-K 0000879407-26-000045, ex. 99.1). The label dose is 25 mg subcutaneously once every 3 months from a prefilled syringe that patients or caregivers are trained to inject (DailyMed setid 7fd37993-f85a-4af1-8bbe-133299f226ed, sections 2.1 and 2.2), so it is a pharmacy-benefit (Part D) product and the Part D convention applies, not the Part B 6% add-on. Gross-to-net 0.5: a gross CMS figure halved lands at a median 96% of CMS's own negotiated net annual prices across the nine cycle-one IRA drugs (backend/gross_to_net.py), the rate lly_solbinsiran.csv takes for the same sHTG pool. 45,000 x (1 - 0.5) = 22,500 USD = 0.0225 mm USD
column12: a convention on a real list price, not a measured net. Why not a realised incumbent price, as regn_veopoz.csv's layers use: drug_demand holds no CMS row for Vascepa, Tryngolza or Redemplo (its latest CMS year is 2024, and Redemplo launched in November 2025 per the FY2026 10-K), and Arrowhead quantifies no gross-to-net (FY2026 10-K 0000879407-26-000078 describes 'Gross-to-Net Adjustments' without a figure). The book's sibling sHTG layer nets Tryngolza's $40,000 WAC to $20,000 (lly_solbinsiran.csv); this is $2,500 above it because Arrowhead prices at what it calls 'a premium to the competing APOC3 inhibitor' (same release). WHICH WAY IT ERRS: high if sHTG payers demand deeper rebates than a one-price FCS and sHTG model allows, since the layer's eligible sHTG pool is 711,850 against 3,401 FCS patients (the rows above); and a full labelled year is billed to every treated patient, while starters and stoppers buy part of one
